## V0.6 — the access control update

The access control update, and support for Minecraft 26.3. Keycards, retinal scanning, the Codebreaker, keypad doors and a version checker — everything that decides who can open what, on top of V0.5's ownership work.

### Added
- **Keycard system** — Keycard Reader and Keycard Lock, keycard levels 1–5, the Limited Use Keycard and Keycard Holder, all with per-owner linking.
- **Retinal Scanner, Scanner Door, Scanner Trapdoor** — opens for whoever the owner allows, by name.
- **Keypad Door, Keypad Trapdoor** — passcode-locked doors on top of V0.5's reinforced door work.
- **Universal Key Changer** — resets a block's passcode or keycard link.
- **Codebreaker** — the attacker's side of the passcode/keycard systems, with its cooldown and failure chance.
- **Version checker** — a chat notification on join when a newer release is out, with a download link.
- **Welcome message** — a short chat message on join, matching the original's "thanks for using SecurityCraft" line.
- **Locking any modded container** *(beyond the original)* — the Key Panel converts a compatible chest into a real keypad chest, same as upstream. For a container it can't convert (a modded chest that doesn't extend `ChestBlock`), it instead locks that position directly — same set/check passcode flow, same ownership enforcement, visible in Jade.

### Changed
- **Universal Block Remover** no longer downgrades a reinforced block to its vanilla counterpart in place — it now instantly destroys and drops the block (you get the reinforced item back), matching the original's actual behaviour. Bypasses the normal, much slower break time same as before.
- **Scanner Door / Scanner Trapdoor** no longer auto-close on a timer by default — they only toggle open/closed when looked at, matching the original. An owner can still opt into a timed auto-close through Customize.

### Fixed
- **Universal Block Remover** had no ownership check at all — anyone could strip a reinforced block's protection.
- **Universal Owner Changer** silently stripped a block's protection when renamed to an offline player — it now resolves the name through the server's profile cache and refuses the transfer if it doesn't resolve to a real account.
- **Scanner/Keycard Reader auto-close** wasn't working at all on the first pass.
- **Retinal Scanner / Scanner Door / Scanner Trapdoor / Keycard Reader / Keycard Lock** couldn't open reinforced doors at all — added the missing door-activator hook.
- **Retinal Scanner** had a transparent hole where its face should render.
- **Keycard Reader GUI** rebuilt to match the original's layout exactly — icons, the Smart Module indicator, signature stepper, and the independent-vs-restricted level toggle logic (was stuck in restricted mode even with a Smart Module installed).
- **Keycard Holder** didn't open at all (missing interaction handler), then opened with the wrong layout — now matches the original's real 5-slot single-row GUI.
- **Key Panel** would briefly ghost-place itself on the floor when locking a modded container, and now refunds itself when a locked container is mined instead of the panel being lost for good.
- **Codebreaker** cooldown, chance, and creative-mode bypass now match the original.
- **SecurityCraft Manual** was missing the crafting-grid recipe for seven V0.6 items (they'd been wrongly flagged as "converted, not crafted").
- **SecurityCraft Manual page count** — restored all missing V0.6 pages (56 pages total across all 16 supported versions).
- **Jade** now shows the owner for a locked modded container, not just that it's protected, and updated for Jade 26.3.5+ compatibility.

...

## V0.6.1 — the access control update

A targeted hotfix release addressing keycard linking disconnects, missing recipe serializers, and door timer persistence across world reloads, alongside the full V0.6 access control update content.

### Fixed
- **Linking a Keycard on the Keycard Reader caused a disconnect with a network encoder error.**
  Clicking "Link" inside the Keycard Reader interface disconnected players with `Internal Exception: io.netty.handler.codec.EncoderException: Failed to encode packet 'clientbound/minecraft:container_set_slot'` and `Can't find id for 'null' in map Registry[minecraft:data_component_type]`. The `KEYCARD_DATA`, `KEYCARD_HOLDER_DATA`, and `CODEBREAKER_LAST_USED` data components were declared but missing from `BuiltInRegistries.DATA_COMPONENT_TYPE` during initialization on affected versions, causing Netty packet encoding to crash when serializing the item stack to the client. Reported by **Jacksonian**.
- **Recipe registration error for `securitycraft:limited_use_keycard_recipe`.**
  The serializer for the Limited Use Keycard recipe was missing from `BuiltInRegistries.RECIPE_SERIALIZER` on several versions (1.21.7, 1.21.8, 1.21.10, 1.21.11), triggering recipe loading errors in the server/client log on startup. Reported by **Jacksonian**.
- **Doors opened by a Retinal Scanner remained stuck open after reloading the world.**
  If a world was saved and reloaded while a door or trapdoor had been triggered open by a Retinal Scanner, active countdown timers were lost, leaving the door open permanently instead of auto-closing. Active power/close timers are now persisted to NBT and auto-reset properly on world load.

### Added in V0.6
- **Keycard system** — Keycard Reader and Keycard Lock, keycard levels 1–5, the Limited Use Keycard and Keycard Holder, all with per-owner linking.
- **Retinal Scanner, Scanner Door, Scanner Trapdoor** — opens for whoever the owner allows, by name.
- **Keypad Door, Keypad Trapdoor** — passcode-locked doors on top of V0.5's reinforced door work.
- **Universal Key Changer** — resets a block's passcode or keycard link.
- **Codebreaker** — the attacker's side of the passcode/keycard systems, with its cooldown and failure chance.
- **Version checker** — a chat notification on join when a newer release is out, with a download link.
- **Welcome message** — a short chat message on join, matching the original's "thanks for using SecurityCraft" line.
- **Locking any modded container** *(beyond the original)* — the Key Panel converts a compatible chest into a real keypad chest, same as upstream. For a container it can't convert, it instead locks that position directly.

## V0.5 — the ownership update

The ownership update. Every reinforced block, door and trapdoor now remembers who placed it, the
Customize screen lets you change a block's modules and options in-game, and 47 more reinforced
blocks join the set — on top of the passcode-protected containers, the crystal quartz set, the
secret signs and the in-game manual.

### Added
- **Ownership** — every reinforced block, door and trapdoor remembers who placed it and can only be
  broken by them. Non-owners break it slower if the config allows breaking it at all, and owners get
  a full-speed break like the original.
- **Team ownership** — a block owned by a player on a scoreboard team is usable by the whole team.
- **Universal Owner Changer** — transfers a block's ownership to whoever the tool is renamed to.
- **Universal Block Modifier** and the **Customize screen** — module slots, per-block options, and a
  toggle to enable or disable an installed module without taking it out.
- **Electrified iron fence and fence gate**.
- **47 further reinforced blocks** — the carpets, glazed terracotta, ladder, lanterns, chain, end
  rod, cobweb, scaffolding, lever, redstone lamp, grass block, podzol, mycelium, sea lantern and
  bookshelf.
- **Functional reinforced blocks** — hopper, dispenser, dropper, observer, pistons, cauldrons,
  lectern and chiseled bookshelf, each keeping its vanilla function while owned.
- **Passcode-protected chest, barrel, furnace, smoker and blast furnace** — converted from their
  vanilla counterpart with a Key Panel, same as the keypad and keypad chest.
- **Crystal quartz set**, plain and reinforced.
- **Secret signs** — standing, wall and hanging, for every wood type.
- **Fake water and fake lava**.
- **SecurityCraft Manual** — the in-game manual, with its recipe pages.
- **Jade integration** — shows a block's owner in the tooltip.

### Fixed
- **The Customize screen** was built from guesswork on the first pass; it has since been rebuilt
  against the original's own layout and wording, with working option buttons and a module button
  that highlights correctly.
- **Ownership after a transfer** could leave a block acting as if nobody owned it; the Universal
  Owner Changer now hands ownership over cleanly and restores the vanilla break speed for the new
  owner.
- **The reinforced door's window** rendered solid black on some versions, and chat message colouring
  around ownership was inconsistent — both fixed.
- **The decoration and technical creative tabs** now match the original's block order.
- **The lens recipe** and the module button highlight were fixed alongside the Customize screen work.

## V0.4 — the explosives update

The explosives update. A whole new creative tab of mines and traps, the Portable Radar, and a long
list of fixes — several of them for things that had been quietly broken since earlier releases.

### Added
- **SecurityCraft: Explosives** — a new creative tab with the full explosives set, in the original's
  order: **42 entries** (**43** on the versions that have the Creaking Heart).
- **Mine** — the classic hidden explosive. Right-click to arm or defuse it; it detonates when an
  entity steps on it.
- **34 disguised mines** — mines that look exactly like an ordinary block until they go off: stone,
  cobblestone, deepslate, dirt, sand, gravel, netherrack, end stone, gilded blackstone, suspicious
  sand and gravel, ancient debris, every ore and its deepslate variant, plus **Furnace**, **Smoker**
  and **Blast Furnace** mines that still work as their real block until triggered.
- **Bouncing Betty** — leaps into the air before exploding, so cover is no help.
- **Claymore** — a directional mine that fires along the way it faces. Takes a **lens** to change the
  colour of its sight line.
- **IMS (Intelligent Munitions System)** — launches homing bombs at intruders, with a configurable
  number of charges. Crafted from a Portable Radar, reinforced iron and Bouncing Betties.
- **Rail Mine** — a rail that explodes when a minecart rides over it.
- **Mine Remote Access Tool** — bind up to six mines by right-clicking them, then arm, defuse,
  detonate or unbind any of them remotely from its screen.
- **Wire Cutters** — shift-right-click a passcode-protected block to convert it back and recover the
  Key Panel.
- **Portable Radar** — detects players in range and messages its owner. Its options (search radius and
  delay, message repeat, team messaging, ignore owner, respect invisibility) are saved and honoured.

### Fixed
- **GUI labels were invisible** on the newer Minecraft versions. They were drawn with the colour
  `4210752`, i.e. `0x00404040`, whose alpha is zero — older versions silently forced such colours
  opaque and newer ones do not. This affected the Universal Block Reinforcer, both passcode screens,
  the colour chooser and the Mine Remote Access Tool.
- **The JEI item list no longer covers the Block Reinforcer's colour chooser** — JEI now knows about
  the popped-out area and moves its list aside, like the original.
- **Converting a Frame into a Keypad** plays the mod's own lock sound instead of a vanilla iron door.
- **Creative tab order** now matches the original — Technical, Explosives, Decoration. Fabric sorts
  custom tabs by their id rather than by registration order, which had put them in the wrong order.
- **Reinforced Dispenser and Dropper** (and their vertical variants) rendered as missing models,
  because the block model parent they refer to had never been added on these versions.
- The **Laser Block recipe on 1.20.1** could not be crafted: it used conventional tags that do not
  exist before 1.20.5, so two of its ingredients were empty.
- The **Reinforced Iron Bars loot table** referred to a loot condition this port does not implement,
  which made the server fail to parse it.
- The **26.x branches could not be built at all** on a machine without Java 25 installed, since they
  had no toolchain repository configured. Gradle now fetches the toolchain itself.
